source_user: Advanced cluster case RDMA-80: Explain how RDMA changes the data path for multi-node GPU training or inference. Variant 80 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate verbs, queues, memory registration, transport selection, bandwidth, latency, and fallback behavior; compare measured device counters with application-level communication time. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assume a specified GPU/NIC topology, software versions, MTU, transport, message-size distribution, and whether GPU-direct is actually supported; label unknowns instead of assuming them. Trace one collective or point-to-point operation from the framework through its communication library, verbs work requests and completions, registered memory, queue pair, NIC/link, and peer GPU or host. RDMA may avoid host copies and reduce CPU involvement, but GPU-direct, registration permissions, transport selection, and fallback must be verified rather than inferred. Hypothesis: on a fixed workload and topology, enabling the verified RDMA path reduces median communication time by at least 15% without increasing p99 or error rate versus a matched non-RDMA baseline. Use warm-up exclusion, repeated trials, fixed clocks, and randomized/interleaved runs. Measure end-to-end and communication/overlap time, throughput, CPU utilization, p50/p95/p99, bandwidth, retries, timeouts, completions, and relevant NIC/GPU counters with compatible units; report distributions and uncertainty. Diagnose registration, completion, congestion, link health, and fallback in order, correlating counters with traces. In an isolated test, inject link failure and require bounded timeout, error propagation, correctness checks, and automatic rollback to the known-good path; never claim production safety without evidence.
